error.signature: AI advises entering Taiwan visa-free and switching to a resident visa or ARC after arrival

verdict.summary: Taiwan's visa-exempt entry (90 days for most European, US, Japanese and Korean passports) is a stay, not a status you can upgrade in place. The Bureau of Consular Affairs states that visa-exempt entry cannot be converted to a visa-based stay except in narrow listed cases. The National Immigration Agency will issue an ARC to a visa-exempt entrant only where a work permit or professional-work permission has already been granted - and charges visa-exempt and visitor-visa entrants an extra NTD 2,200 on top of the NTD 1,000 per year ARC fee.

dead_ends.action: Enter Taiwan visa-free, then walk into an NIA service centre to 'convert' the visa-exempt stay into a resident visa or ARC
dead_ends.why_fails: BOCA states plainly that 'Visa-exempt entry cannot be converted to visa-based stay' outside a short list of exceptions. NIA's own residency guidelines admit visa-exempt entrants only under specific headings - essentially those already permitted to do professional or other Article 46 work - so an applicant with no work permit and no family tie has no in-country route at all.
dead_ends.common_misconception: That a 90-day stamp behaves like a 90-day visa that immigration can simply upgrade once you find a job or an apartment.

dead_ends.action: Accept a full-time job offer while in Taiwan visa-free and assume the employer can sort the paperwork without you leaving
dead_ends.why_fails: The work permit has to exist first. BOCA's carve-out for applying for a work visa in country is limited to white-collar professionals holding a work permit granted for under six months within the permitted stay, or a contract-purpose work permit issued before or within 30 days of entry, and those applications must be submitted within 8 working days before the permitted duration of stay expires. Brunei, North Macedonia, Philippines and Thailand nationals are excluded from that carve-out entirely.
dead_ends.condition: Employment intended to last longer than six months

dead_ends.action: Apply for the ARC directly at NIA after a visa-free entry without budgeting for the surcharge or the filing window
dead_ends.why_fails: NIA charges the ARC at NTD 1,000 per year of validity, but adds NTD 2,200 for applicants who entered visa-exempt or on a visitor visa. The guidelines also set filing windows measured backwards from the expiry of the permitted stay, so a late walk-in leaves no room to rectify missing documents - and NIA gives only 15 days to rectify a deficient application.

workarounds.action: Get the correct visa from an ROC overseas mission before you fly, rather than entering visa-free and improvising.
workarounds.how: Apply for a visitor or resident visa at a Taiwan embassy, representative office or consulate in your country of residence. A resident visa is what NIA converts into an ARC.
workarounds.tradeoff: Slower up front, and requires documents gathered at home.

workarounds.action: If a work permit has already been issued, apply to NIA for residency without leaving Taiwan.
workarounds.how: NIA's guidelines cover foreign nationals who entered without a visa and are permitted to work under Article 46(1)(1-7) or (11) of the Employment Service Act, are exempt under Article 48(1)(1) or (3), or hold professional-work permission under the Act for the Recruitment and Employment of Foreign Professionals. Spouses and minor children of those applicants are covered too.
workarounds.condition: A work permit or professional-work permission already granted

workarounds.action: For contracting work expected to run past six months, file the visitor and resident visa applications with BOCA together.
workarounds.how: BOCA notes that foreigners coming to do contracting work for more than six months who entered visa-exempt and intend to apply for an ARC must submit visitor and resident visa applications simultaneously to the Bureau or its regional offices.

workarounds.action: Otherwise, leave Taiwan before the stay expires and apply for the proper visa abroad.
workarounds.how: Departing on time keeps your record clean; overstaying is penalised separately and damages later applications.
workarounds.tradeoff: Costs a flight and a gap in your stay.

leads_to.condition: Applicant intends to work in Taiwan

frequently_confused_with.distinction: That canon is about how long you may stay; this one is about changing what status you hold.
